native_catalog.name: blender
native_catalog.description: Build, edit, animate and render 3D content in Blender with Python (bpy), usually headless. Covers modeling objects and assemblies from a description or reference image, recreating a photographed scene, laying out environments from a tabletop to a landscape or city, animation (keyframes, paths, physics, camera moves), lighting, materials and still or video renders, each checked with renders. Use whenever a task involves Blender, bpy, a .blend file, 3D modeling, a procedural 3D scene, or rendering a 3D image or animation. Matching a reference image requires its critic loop: when the workflow tool is available, launch the shipped workflows/critic_loop.js right after viewing the reference (it builds, then runs blind critic rounds and fixes); otherwise an observation sheet, then every round a blind review and seven specific critics, until `critic.py check` passes.

native_catalog.name: game-3d-visuals
native_catalog.description: Use for 3D work where the user wants a polished, art-directed look: recreating an object or scene from reference image(s), modeling and rendering in Blender, or an explicit ask for high visual fidelity in a three.js, WebGL/WebGPU or game-engine scene. It adds consistent reference images, a detailed visual PRD, a blockout gate and a render-vs-reference acceptance loop, run as a fixed Workflow script when the workflow tool is available, which takes much longer than a direct build. Skip it for quick prototypes or playable pages where a fast working result matters more, small edits, and 2D work. When it applies, read it before tool-specific skills such as blender or threejs and use those for technique.
